summary: Lets ORDER BY refer to an unqualified common column of a NATURAL or USING join by moving expandCommonColumn from Expander to SqlValidatorImpl, calling it for ORDER BY items, and teaching AggChecker to match GROUP BY items through an AS wrapper.

tests.evidence: Bug fix with validator, SqlToRel, and join.iq tests (validated against PostgreSQL); a focused pass should check cases such as a select alias that shadows the common column and FULL JOIN with aggregates.

user_docs.evidence: Bug fix making standard SQL work; no option or documented behavior.

doc_comments.evidence: mihaibudiu found that the comment in expandExprFromJoin ('must be NATURAL or USING here') was wrong since ON joins reach it; the author rewrote it, and the final version adds a comment in checkRollUpInSelectList.

change_description.evidence: PR body is only the Jira link; title matches the Jira, and the rationale was given in review comments instead.

backward_compat.evidence: Queries that failed with an ambiguity error now validate; the moved method was on a package-private nested class, so no public API changes.

error_model.evidence: The 'Column is ambiguous' error no longer fires for common columns in ORDER BY; ON joins must still report it, which the reviewer discussion confirmed.

correctness.evidence: Non-trivial name-resolution change; reviewer found a redundant branch and questioned double expansion and the AggChecker equalsDeep/AS handling. validateOrderList expands common columns before regular expansion, which may bypass select-alias precedence in ORDER BY.

surprising_behavior.evidence: ORDER BY resolution order changes (common-column expansion runs before alias resolution), which a user might notice when an alias shares the column name.

contradictions.evidence: Inherited comment contradicted the code path; covered by doc_comments.

spec_conformance.evidence: Implements SQL-standard semantics of NATURAL/USING common columns in ORDER BY (COALESCE for FULL JOIN, which side for LEFT/RIGHT); the author checked against PostgreSQL.

plan.why: One cohesive validator change where correctness, SQL semantics, tests, and comments all concern the same resolution path.
